By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How low can you go

Summary:
Meet the charismatic crook Alwyn Smit who was Old Mututal's top insurance broker. Also meet his sidekick, another top old mutual broker, Mr Thiart. Both prayed on vulnerable woman and widows. In Alwyn's case, he would persuade the 91 woman he dealt with to sell their properties so he could invest their money. But he ran an investment scam by withdrawing these investments on a regular basis, reinvesting them and making handsome fees. He also ran a small ponzi scheme as well and he also funneled his ill gotten gains into a personal retirement fund. He scammed 66 million rand from women who are now destitute and in some cases suicidal. When Old Mutual discovered what was going on, they sequestrated him had him debarred. Alwyn at present sells Kia motor cars and is due in a few years to get that pension fund worth about 6 million rand. Now the struggle starts to have that pension fund money taken away from him and reimbursed to his victims. Part of this story will look at this and how old Mutual have not exactly been helpful.

Mr Thiart would befriend elderly women at death's door in old age homes. He would gain their trust and support by being a charming new friend who would get their power of attorneys and when they died he would clear their banks out.

Press Release:


Savings Lost
He was a top investment broker, earning massive commissions. Clients and friends trusted him. Alwyn Smit led the high-life, but seemingly at the expense of others. After sequestration in 2014, tragic tales of how he allegedly took advantage of vulnerable clients emerged. Court records show that R25-million of their money disappeared. One client who lost R3-million now survives on handouts. Another had to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital after losing her entire savings of R4-million. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


In April 2012, Mrs. Henna Smith was murdered in her home in Citrusdal. She left

R600 000 to her son Isak. He and his wife instructed their sympathetic

insurance broker to invest that money in an Old Mutual policy. Something he

never did. That money is gone.

Renette Smit: I was shocked. I felt betrayed.

Three years ealier, the Paarl community in the Cape was devastated by a tragic

fire at Paarl Printers which claimed the lives of 13 employees.

LINK: One of the widows authorized an insurance broker to invest her late

husbands life insurance policy, which amounted to about R860 000. Now

all of it has gone.

This is the story of an insurance broker turned car salesman.

LINK: So who are we talking about? Well his name is Alwyn Bernadus Smit.

He was a franchised agent for Old Mutual and at one time was their top

broker earning massive commissions.

A former Pollsmoor prison warden, Smit changed careers and became a top

insurance broker with hundreds of clients selling mainly retirement annuities

and long-term investments. He was a franchised old mutual broker from 2011 to

2013. He was well liked and respected.

John: What kind of person is Alwyn? Was he somebody that you always

trusted?

Renette: Yes we did, we did. For so long, yes we did. Fully.

Billy: He is a nice guy if you meet him. He is always friendly, helpful.

Former friend Billy Jacobs, recalls a night when Smit opened up his computer to

show him how much money he was making.

and he showed me the earnings for that specific month and it was over

R750 000.

John: What company was that?

Billy: Old Mutual.

Link: Judging by these court papers, Smit had quite a spending habit. He

was able to blow 44 million since 2008. We’re talking fast cars, fancy

properties, including one in the upmarket Fancourt and wait for it, an

aeroplane.

This is the beachcraft plane he bought for about 2 million rand. It seems that this

high flyers lifestyle was funded at the expense of some of his clients. Annike

Gouws was once a long time client and friend of Smit. For several years she even

cared for one of his children. She lost her life savings of 3 million rands after

smit advised her to sell her properties for better investments. That money

disappeared leaving her destitute.

Annike Gouws: I’ve lost so much. What’s the purpose now of life?

Today, she and her brother share a granny flat surviving on handouts. Her small

state pension does not even cover the rent of over R3000 rand rent per month.

She is devastated.

LINK: Another of smits alleged victims had a breakdown when 4 million

rand of her life savings, which she had given him to invest on her behalf,

simply vannished. She was admitted here to the Valkenburg psychiatric

hospital in Cape Town. These tragic stories came to light when old mutual

began investigating complaints against him in 2013.

They had him debarred for Churning, the industry term for reinvesting client’s

policies to gain additional commissions. They also had him declared insolvent in

march 2014. Planet Administrators were appointed as trustees. The trustee

report said that an investigation revealed that smit was running a pyramid or

ponzi scheme – that he used at least 4o bank accounts – and that almost 25

million rand worth of invetorss money was lost. It also stated that Smit used

investor’s funs to keep his own and his company’s overfafts down.

Reneatte: He said to me pay that amount into my personal bank account

because that is going to be quicker to give you the contract.

John: No red flags?

Reneatte: I didn’t doubt him for a minute.

After paying into his account she never received her old mutual contract. She

confronted him on one of his visits.

Reneatte: And he said well he is so sorry. He’s got some problems with Old

Mutual and there is no money – the money is just gone.

Even long terms friends fell into his trap. Billy Jacobs even took out a bond to

help Smit after being promised high interest returns. In terms of the insolvency

act, he has to return that interest and some capital he received because it was

paid from other investors’ funds.

John: What would losing more than R700 000 mean for your future?

Billy: Well I never had a house bond. Now I will have a bond. He’s murdered

my pension days. He’s killed my pension days.

But it doesn’t stop there. After Smit was debarred, Marius Walters took over his

old Mutual franchise and offered to purchase one of Smit’s cars as he was

apparently struggling to make monthly payments.

Marius: We agreed that we go to a lawyer and just draft a sales agreement

that I buy the car from him. I pay it into his company. That company he

owned and he will then settle with BMW finance and he would release the

registration documents to me.

But he never handed over that money to BWM SA who then repossessed the car

from Marius.

Marius: My car is gone and my money is gone.

R500 000 lost. An incensed Marius laid charges against Smit who in the mean

time had found a job selling Kia motor cars in Durbanville. He was arrested for

theft.. The case is still pending.

John (phone): Alwyn good afternoon to you. It is John Webb calling from

Carte Blanche. How are you doing?

We spoke to alwyn smit but he said that he would not answer our questions or

give an on camera.

Alwyn (Phone): Well what I did is I talked to the curators and they told me

that it is not necessary for me doing that.

LINK: All of this must be incredibly embarrassing for Old Mutual after all it

was one of their franchise agents who caused all this heartache and misery.

We requested an on camera interview with them on a number of occasions

but they declined.

Instead Old Mtual responded in writing saying that that they sympathize with

Smit’s customers. They added that they employ 6500 advisers nationally and

that “the vast majority of our customers receive good financial advice and

services from our advisors.” Smit was an isolated incident they said.

Now to date the trustees have managed to recover 15 million rand from Smit’s

estate which will go mainly towards paying his bond holders, hp creditors and

costs. Leaving very little ,,,,, for the victims at this stage.

LINK: And now the irony of the story. It seems that Alwyn Smit has quite a

nest egg built up in an Old Mutual retirement fund but that money is

protected by the pension funds act. We understand that old mutual and the

trustees have had to negotiate with Smit to have some of that money

released to compensate his victims.

According to court records Smit has 6.5 million rand in his retirement pension

fund. But he has only agreed to release 1. 24 million rand to compensate victims.

The trustees have spend a 100 000 rand in legal fees to see if they could get hold

of all of his pension fund investments but with no luck. Attorney Jonathan Mort

is an expert on the pension fund act and explains why these investments are so

protected.

Jonathan Mort: All retirement savings are intended to be protected from

their debtors and so we have a protection completely against with very

limited exceptions, monies owed to the receiver of revenue, maintenance

payments, housing loans.

It seems possible then that money can be laundered into retirement funds and

be protected. Jonathan believes that the pension fund act should be amended if

there is a strong suspicion that investments are from ill-gotten gains.

Jonathan Mort: because of the fact that they could be seen as a safe haven

for ill gotten gains it would make much more sense if somebody alleging

that the proceeds were in those retirement annuities came form ill gotten

gains If the recipient, the member of the retirement annuity fund, was then

himself required to show that they were not the proceeds. I think that that

would be a big step forward.

Now Old Mutual has listed themselves as a creditor, for about four million rand,

which means that they are also in line to share any monies that the trustees still

recover from Smit’ estate. We quote them:

: “it also suffered damages or losses by reason of Smit’s actions and are entitled

and obliged vis a vis its shareholders to lodge valid claims against the insolvent

estate.”

Renette and her husband believe that the onus is on old mutual to pay them out

in full .

Renette: He was a worker or a consultant form Old Mutual. He was on their

payroll. I think they should contact me and I think they should help me to

get hold of that R600 000.

.

It been 18 months since mrs Annetjie Gouws leant that she had lost all her

money, plunging into her present situation. She’s barely holding out…

Annike Gouws: I wont do anything to my life but I don’t have anything to

live for anymore.

Old Mutual said that they “ we will compensate customers where the fact and

circumstances show that we are vicariously liable for looses suffered by

customers due to smit’s actions: They will treat each case on its merit.

Some investors have laid charges and the hawks are investigating.

Jonathan Mort: because of the fact that they could be seen as a safe haven for ill gotten gains it would make much more sense if somebody alleging that the proceeds were in those retirement annuities came form ill gotten gains If the recipient, the member of the retirement annuity fund, was then himself required to show that they were not the proceeds. I think that that would be a big step forward. Now Old Mutual has listed themselves as a creditor, for about four million rand, which means that they are also in line to share any monies that the trustees still recover from Smit’ estate. We quote them: : “it also suffered damages or losses by reason of Smit’s actions and are entitled and obliged vis a vis its shareholders to lodge valid claims against the insolvent estate.” Renette and her husband believe that the onus is on old mutual to pay them out in full . Renette: He was a worker or a consultant form Old Mutual. He was on their payroll. I think they should contact me and I think they should help me to get hold of that R600 000. . It been 18 months since mrs Annetjie Gouws leant that she had lost all her money, plunging into her present situation. She’s barely holding out… Annike Gouws: I wont do anything to my life but I don’t have anything to live for anymore. Old Mutual said that they “ we will compensate customers where the fact and circumstances show that we are vicariously liable for looses suffered by customers due to smit’s actions: They will treat each case on its merit. Some investors have laid charges and the hawks are investigating. metadata.Summary: Meet the charismatic crook Alwyn Smit who was Old Mututal's top insurance broker. Also meet his sidekick, another top old mutual broker, Mr Thiart. Both prayed on vulnerable woman and widows. In Alwyn's case, he would persuade the 91 woman he dealt with to sell their properties so he could invest their money. But he ran an investment scam by withdrawing these investments on a regular basis, reinvesting them and making handsome fees. He also ran a small ponzi scheme as well and he also funneled his ill gotten gains into a personal retirement fund. He scammed 66 million rand from women who are now destitute and in some cases suicidal. When Old Mutual discovered what was going on, they sequestrated him had him debarred. Alwyn at present sells Kia motor cars and is due in a few years to get that pension fund worth about 6 million rand. Now the struggle starts to have that pension fund money taken away from him and reimbursed to his victims. Part of this story will look at this and how old Mutual have not exactly been helpful. Mr Thiart would befriend elderly women at death's door in old age homes. He would gain their trust and support by being a charming new friend who would get their power of attorneys and when they died he would clear their banks out.
